newsitem.title: USA: AccuMed says FDA responds to application.
newsitem.headline: AccuMed says FDA responds to application.

text.p: AccuMed International Inc said Tuesday it received a response from the U.S. Food & Drug Administration regarding its new product application for the AccuMed TracCell 2000 system.
AccuMed said the FDA raised "administrative-type questions," to which it believes it is already in a position to respond.

"I am gratified that, in no instance, were there any requests for additional prospective studies to be undertaken," Norman Pressman, president of AccuMed's Cytopathology Division, said in a statement.
AccuMed said the response after only 88 days is "significantly ahead" of FDA's average response schedule.

Peter Gombrich, chairman of AccuMed, said the response received from the FDA contained "no surprises," adding the agency did not raise any issues that would cause major concern for AccuMed to comply with and respond to in a timely manner.
The TracCell 2000 is a fully automated slide mapping system used in Pap testing.
AccuMed International is a global laboratory diagnostic products company.
